:::{#rem-matvec-row-dot-products}
#### Each entry is a dot product

Matrix-vector multiplication extends the dot product (@def-dot-product):
entry $i$ of $\matr{A}\vx$ is the dot product of row $i$ of $\matr{A}$
with $\vx$.
For example,

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd (-1) \\ 3 \cd 1 + 4 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

:::
